subject: Egress segmentation and firewall port-scope review for private connector
messages:
From: Ross Tanner <ross.tanner@weavecorp.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: secops@weavecorp.com
Date: 2027-02-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private endpoint allowlist and port scoping questions

Hi Sofia,

We're about to schedule the on-prem connector roll-out for WeaveCorp's analytics cluster. Before we open the ticket with Network, SecOps asked for a concise allowlist and port-scope they can hand to our firewall team and change-control. A couple of things they called out:

- We need a single source of truth for remote IP ranges (control plane / telemetry / metrics).
- We need clarity on whether DNS (UDP/TCP 53) or other UDP flows are required to the public internet, or if DNS can be proxied.
- Any mTLS requirements (client certs) vs. standard TLS to public endpoints.

Can you provide a short matrix with: IP ranges, FQDNs, ports (L4), protocol (TCP/UDP), expected connection direction (outbound only), SNI/domain to allow, and whether inspection / TLS break is allowed?

We'd like the matrix and an ops-friendly explanation to give to our change board by EOW.

Thanks,
Ross
Ross Tanner
WeaveCorp - Platform Security

On Mon, Feb 1, 2027 at 08:50 AM Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com> wrote:
> (internal note from discovery call attached)
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ross Tanner <ross.tanner@weavecorp.com>, WeaveCorp Security <secops@weavecorp.com>
Date: 2027-02-01T12:45:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Private endpoint allowlist and port scoping questions

Hi team — looping you in. Ross's ask is straightforward but WeaveCorp's security team prefers a minimal L4 footprint and prefers DNS/proxying to break out UDP where possible.

Draft constraints / decisions we should validate with Infra + Security:

1) Control plane + model pulls (outbound TLS):
   - IPs: 198.51.100.32/27 (control plane egress set)
   - FQDNs: controlplane.redwood-inference.net, api-models.redwood-inference.net
   - Ports: TCP 443 (primary); TCP 8443 (optional for mTLS/metrics)
   - TLS: standard TLS 1.2+ acceptable for API traffic; OAuth bearer token auth.
   - SNI: allowlist by hostname; do not rely on IP-only rules if customer wants hostnames.
   - Notes: We support mTLS for private deployments on 8443 for customers with scoped HSM/KMS requirements.

2) Telemetry & Metrics (optional separate path):
   - IPs: 198.51.100.64/27 (telemetry pool)
   - Ports: TCP 443 for secure ingestion; TCP 9091 for Prometheus push (if opt-in).
   - Direction: outbound only; firewall should permit connection initiation from on-prem connector to telemetry endpoints.

3) DNS and resolution:
   - Recommendation: Block direct UDP/53 to internet. Route DNS via corporate recursive resolvers or an HTTP(S) DNS proxy.
   - If customer will not proxy DNS, allow UDP/TCP 53 only to the resolver IP(s) they control.

4) CRL/OCSP and Certificate Validation:
   - Allow outbound HTTPS to ocsp-responder.redwood-inference.net (TCP 443) for cert revocation checks.

5) Health checks / keepalives:
   - IPs: use control plane pool above. Keepalive connections will be long-lived; stateful firewall must allow established flows back from remote ephemeral ports.

Open items for David / Marissa to confirm:
- Exact ephemeral NAT IP range we will request (customer asks for a CIDR to pin to their perimeter).
- Whether we should publish a second-tier fallback IP range for capacity failover.

I'll prepare an ops-ready matrix and a one-page narrative for their change board. David — can you draft the matrix and include a short note on TLS inspection compatibility (we don't support break-and-inspect for mTLS flows).

Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ross Tanner <ross.tanner@weavecorp.com>, WeaveCorp Security <secops@weavecorp.com>
Date: 2027-02-02T08:03:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Private endpoint allowlist and port scoping questions

Folks — attached is the first-pass matrix (redwood-egress-port-matrix-v1.xlsx) and a short text file with example proxy snippets (egress-proxy-snippets.txt). Highlights:

- Control plane (API): 198.51.100.32/27, TCP 443 (SNI: controlplane.redwood-inference.net).
- Control plane (mTLS option): 198.51.100.40/30, TCP 8443 (client cert expected).
- Telemetry: 198.51.100.64/27, TCP 443.
- Ephemeral NAT pool for customer pinning: 203.0.113.16/28 (we can reserve 16 addresses for their change board; these are the public egress addresses they will see).
- DNS guidance: prefer resolver-proxy on port 53 to customer resolver; alternatively, allow UDP/TCP 53 only to the resolver IPs in the spreadsheet.
- Ports to avoid allowing through transparent TLS inspection: 8443 (mTLS) and 9091 (if using plaintext metrics).

Operational notes for WeaveCorp firewall team (short):
- All connections are outbound from the on-prem connector. Stateful inspection must be configured to allow established responses.
- Do not NAT controlplane IPs behind a shared ephemeral pool unless you can reserve the 203.0.113.16/28 range for us — otherwise the control plane will see mixed customer IPs and Ops will have trouble correlating traffic.
- For SNI-based allowlisting, ensure your perimeter proxies forward SNI without modification; if they strip/override SNI, fall back to IP allowlist.

Attachments (referenced in the workbook): example iptables snippets, FQDN wildcard handling, and an Ops checklist for update window timing.

If this looks good I can tighten wording for their RFC and produce a one-page sign-off doc for their CAB.

-David
David Kim
Network Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Ross Tanner <ross.tanner@weavecorp.com>, WeaveCorp Security <secops@weavecorp.com>
Cc: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-03T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Private endpoint allowlist and port scoping questions — proposed matrix and CAB wording

Hi Ross / SecOps team,

Thanks for the patience — attached is our proposed RFC-ready matrix (redwood-egress-port-matrix-v1.xlsx) and a short operations narrative. Summary (TL;DR):

- Minimum allowlist: TCP 443 to controlplane.redwood-inference.net (198.51.100.32/27) + TCP 443 to telemetry pool (198.51.100.64/27).
- Optional (if you require mTLS): TCP 8443 to 198.51.100.40/30 (client certs required).
- DNS: we strongly recommend routing DNS through your corporate recursive resolvers or an HTTPS DNS proxy — do not allow wildcard UDP/53 to the internet.
- Ephemeral egress addresses: 203.0.113.16/28 (customer-visible NAT range). Please request these be reserved during the maintenance window if you need IP pinning.

Failure modes and mitigations:
- If DNS UDP/53 is blocked with no proxy: the connector will fail hostname resolution; mitigation: configure internal resolver or fallback to HTTP-based DNS.
- If TLS inspectors perform break-and-inspect on mTLS endpoints (8443): client cert verification will fail — mitigation: keep mTLS traffic exempt from TLS interception or move mTLS to an internal-only path.

Next steps we recommend for your CAB:
1) Network approves the CIDR reservations above.
2) Security approves TLS-inspection carve-outs (8443/mTLS).
3) Schedule a 30-minute pre-cut with Redwood SRE during the maintenance window to validate NAT visibility and certificate chains.

If you confirm the CAB items we will provide a short sign-off blurb you can paste into the change ticket.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-egress-port-matrix-v1.xlsx (workbook), egress-proxy-snippets.txt (iptables + proxy examples)
